messages:
eli-cs: Heads-up — Acme onboarding hit a spike of 429s during SDK init this morning. They say it starts right after they exchange ephemeral creds. Seen similar with preflight fanout before. :frowning:
sam-eng: Can you paste the exact init flow they run? small code snippets help. 429s or 401s?
eli-cs: 429s mainly. Sequence is: 1) request ephemeral from our /v1/ephemeral -> gets short-lived token 2) client parallel preflight calls to /v1/generate (50+ in 2s) 
maya-ops: 50 parallel preflights is a stampede. Do we return `Retry-After` on those 429s?
eli-cs: They get a standard 429 with no `Retry-After` header in some cases. I asked them to dump response headers. Repro snippet they shared:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \/ -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL" \/ -d '{"model":"rwd-3-small","prompt":"hi"}'
```

sam-eng: Two quick items: 1) client should jitter/backoff (exponential) for preflight burst; 2) ephemeral token TTL might be too short causing concurrent refresh work. Can you confirm TTL and whether they rotate tokens on every request?
eli-cs: They rotate per session, but their SDK demo rotates per button click in parallel web workers. TTL is 45s according to their logs.
maya-ops: 45s TTL + aggressive parallel refresh = heavy auth backend load. Also clock drift can cause auth failures when signature windows are tight. Ask them to check client clock vs NTP and to add a 1–2s skew tolerance.
eli-cs: I asked them to run `ntpstat` and they reported client VM skew of ~6s. They pushed a fix to sync and retested — 429s dropped ~70% but still see burst tail.
sam-eng: For the remaining tail, propose two mitigations we can recommend now: 1) on SDK side, implement preflight coalescing: dedupe identical token fetches within 200ms window; 2) on server side, emit `Retry-After` on capacity 429s and include a human-readable `x-rate-class` header so clients can choose slower backoff for auth bursts.
eli-cs: Can we add `x-rate-class` quickly? That would help customers tune heuristics.
maya-ops: We can wire `x-rate-class` as low/med/high in the gateway layer. I'll open an ops ticket to enable it on the preflight path with a 48-hr target. :+1:
sam-eng: Also sending sample JS retry snippet to share with Acme (use jitter + cap):

```
async function retryFetch(opts, max=5){
  for(let i=0;i<max;i++){
    try{return await fetch(opts)}catch(e){
      const wait = Math.min(1000*Math.pow(2,i) * (0.5+Math.random()/2), 5000);
      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, wait));
    }
  }
}
```

eli-cs: Sharing that now. I'm also giving them a short-term workaround: stagger token refresh with random 0-3s delay in web workers and bump ephemeral TTL to 2m for onboarding customer trial accounts.
deploy-bot: deployment started: feature/ratelabel-gateway -> canary on gateway-ops-03 (sha: b7f4c2)
eli-cs: Nice — thanks. I'll coordinate with Acme and confirm next run.
maya-ops: If useful, we can also whitelist their trial key onto a higher burst quota for 48h while they onboard. Ping me with tenant id.
eli-cs: Sending tenant id in DM. Will update thread after their next test. :thumbsup:
